item.title: Father accused of striking son up to 15 times at dental clinic
item.description: A 54-year-old man from Bangladesh has pleaded not guilty to assaulting his son at a dental clinic after the child became frightened of an injection. The dentist told police the man struck the child between 10 and 15 times. The court granted a protection order in favour of the minor until he testifies, and released the father on bail with a 500 deposit, a 2,000 personal guarantee and a requirement to reside at an alternative address.

item.title: Caravan and coach catch fire in Żabbar
item.description: A caravan and a coach caught fire in Żabbar, confirmed by the Civil Protection Department. Details of the blaze remained limited, with the cause not yet established, and it was unclear at the time of publication whether anyone was injured or how extensively the vehicles were damaged. Further information was expected as the investigation proceeds.

item.title: Calls grow for justice reform after acquittals as PN MP accuses Attorney General of weakening her office
item.description: Nationalist Party MP Mark Anthony Sammut has accused Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg of having intentionally weakened her office, saying the prosecution service has lost three jury trials in two months, including Lorin Sciclunas acquittal in the Lassana Cisse race-hate murder case and Yorgen Fenechs acquittal over the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia. Sammut claimed the AGs office has lost veteran lawyers, hired only trainees and left the deputy AG post vacant, and described Buttigieg as corrupt and incompetent. Separately, the Repubblika NGO published a discussion paper, Justice in the Name of the People, calling for research, consultation and reform of Maltas criminal justice system and jury system. MaltaToday separately answered legal questions on the Scicluna verdict, including how he could be convicted without firing the gun, why Francesco Fenech will be tried separately, and what punishment he faces when sentenced on Wednesday.

item.title: Worker injured at Żebbuġ demolition site; BCA and OHSA order all works halted
item.description: A worker was injured during demolition works at a construction site in Sqaq No. 1, Triq Ħal-Dwieli, Żebbuġ. The Building and Construction Authority and the Occupational Health and Safety Authority said in a joint statement on Tuesday that officers went to the site together with police and first aid services. The authorities ordered all construction work at the site to stop while investigations continue, and the workers condition was not yet known.

item.title: Experts investigate construction history of historic palaces
item.description: Heritage Malta, in collaboration with the European COST Action EUROGLOSS, has concluded a two-day international workshop titled Palaces Beyond the Written Source: The Case Study of Malta. Held on 23 and 24 October, it brought together architectural and construction historians, archaeologists, archivists and conservation experts from across Europe to explore new ways of studying historical palatial buildings where written records are incomplete or missing.

item.title: Man admits assaulting partner after police stop car on Coast Road
item.description: A 44-year-old man from Mellieħa admitted assaulting his partner after Rapid Intervention Unit officers found their car stopped in the middle of the Coast Road at about 1am on Monday. The woman told officers her partner punched her in the chin, struck her with a mobile phone and pushed her against a metal barrier during an argument in Paceville. He was charged with assault, causing slight injuries, intimidation and recidivism, and given bail against a 1,000 deposit and 5,000 personal guarantee with probation support.

item.title: 15-year-old boy charged with injuring mother during family argument
item.description: A 15-year-old boy has been charged with assaulting his mother after an argument over his wish to get a tattoo allegedly turned violent at the family home in Żabbar. He pleaded not guilty to slightly injuring his mother, insulting both parents and causing them fear of violence. Police were called at about 2am on Tuesday; the boy was arrested around 3am. A protection order was granted and he was barred from approaching or contacting either parent.

item.title: Government launches public transport survey under Malta in Motion
item.description: The Ministry for Sustainable Mobility has launched a public survey called Your Journey, Your Say to examine how people travel across Malta, the problems commuters face and what would encourage them to switch from driving. The survey, part of the Malta in Motion programme, opened on 2 November and runs for four weeks, taking about 15 minutes for residents and five for visitors. Results will be combined with existing transport data and published early next year, feeding into the 15-year plan that includes the proposed 2.8 billion light rail line linking the airport to St Pauls Bay.

item.title: Enemalta cable works to close Sliema seafront bus lane for two months
item.description: Enemalta begins works on Wednesday to lay a new 4.5km 11kV cable from the Manoel Island distribution centre in Gżira to the Sliema Ferries area, plus 2.7km of low-voltage cables. The bus lane along the seafront will be closed for excavation and cable-laying and traffic out of Sliema reduced to one lane. Enemalta said the existing cable had accumulated numerous joints over the years and had become increasingly vulnerable to faults.

item.title: Malta Tourism Authority carried out over 1,200 inspections in three localities
item.description: The Malta Tourism Authority carried out more than 1,200 inspections in San Pawl il-Baħar, Tas-Sliema and San Ġiljan, Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela told parliament in reply to a question by MP Graziella Galea. More than 500 of the inspections were carried out in Tas-Sliema, the highest number of the three localities.

item.title: Ian Borg meets King Charles III at Commonwealth summit
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg met King Charles III during the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, describing the meeting as an opportunity to renew the friendships that unite the Commonwealth. Malta is among the Commonwealths member states, with the gathering bringing together representatives to discuss shared priorities and international cooperation.

item.title: Xjenza Malta steps up investment in cultural heritage research
item.description: Xjenza Malta has increased its investment in research into Maltas cultural heritage, which it says is part of the countrys identity and includes historic buildings, archaeological sites, underwater heritage, traditional skills and cultural practices. The agency said climate change and rising environmental pressures make the preservation of that heritage a significant challenge, underscoring the need for sustained research investment.

item.title: Three men jailed for six months over false travel documents
item.description: Mourtda Kasime Jaoud, 33, and Mohammed Hasan Mohammed Al Baaj, 24, both from Iraq, and Sakhr Al Gumaei, 36, from Yemen, pleaded guilty to possessing false travel documents after arriving in Malta on 2 November. Two held false Iraqi passports and the third carried Greek documents belonging to someone else. Magistrate Nadine Sant Lia sentenced each to six months imprisonment.

item.title: Nurses union asks government to exempt health workers from budget measures
item.description: The Malta Union of Midwives and Nurses has asked the government to exempt healthcare staff from Budget 2027 measures that increased their financial burden, requesting an urgent meeting. Around 1,200 third-country national nurses have written to the union with their concerns. Measures include removal of free childcare and free public transport for third-country nationals and higher driving-licence fees, which MUMN says threaten the health and elderly-care sectors.

item.title: 20 people died from excessive heat during July heatwave
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg told parliament that 20 people died from hyperthermia during Julys heatwave, with 179 patients treated at Mater Dei. The figures were given in reply to a question by MP Darren Carabott on how many people were admitted with hyperthermia and how many died. Hyperthermia occurs when the body overheats and cannot cool itself effectively.

item.title: Ten domestic violence arrest warrants still outstanding
item.description: Ten arrest warrants linked to domestic violence cases remain unexecuted in Malta, Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield confirmed in parliament. Eight of the suspects are either abroad or untraceable, while two are receiving treatment at Mount Carmel Hospital. The information was tabled in reply to a question by MP Miriana Calleja Testaferrata de Noto.

item.title: Libya seeks extradition of Lilu King from Malta
item.description: The Libyan government has formally requested the extradition of Mohammed El Mushraty, known as Lilu King, from Malta. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the request was submitted in writing in September, and that all options are being considered before a final decision is taken.

item.title: Survey finds majority of residents see no change in household finances from budget
item.description: A new independent survey by Marketing Advisory Services found 54.4% of Maltese residents said the budget measures made no notable difference to their household finances, while 34.2% said the measures improved their situation. Respondents prioritised cheaper prices for food and essential goods (42.3%), with the survey carried out as debate on Budget 2027 continues.

item.title: Mġarr ix-Xini valley rehabilitation works completed
item.description: Rehabilitation and clean-up works at Mġarr ix-Xini Valley, carried out over the summer to improve rainwater management, have been completed. The works covered about a kilometre from Triq Tal-Gruwa to the existing dam, removing vegetation from around 11,700 square metres and some 24,500 cubic metres of sediment. Gozo Minister Clint Camilleri said the intervention was intended to strengthen the valleys capacity to handle rainwater.

item.title: Tourists spending less despite record arrivals, Alex Borg says
item.description: Speaking at the Nationalist Partys Business Breakfast on Budget 2027, opposition leader Alex Borg said average tourist spending has fallen from 919 in 2015 to 771 in 2025 despite four million visitors in 2025. Citing Chamber of Commerce figures, he said rising visitor numbers are not translating into greater economic value while adding pressure on infrastructure, the environment and public services.

item.title: Freeport ordered to pay 35,000 to injured crane operator
item.description: Crane operator Roderick Bonnici was awarded 35,000 in damages after a 2020 workplace injury at the Birżebbuġa freeport facility. He was hurt when the cranes trolley suddenly lost control, jolting his cabin and injuring his leg and knee. Malta Freeport denied responsibility, but the court, presided over by Judge Henri Mizzi, found an abnormal deceleration had caused the incident.

item.title: Non-EU families put baby plans on hold as childcare centres fear closure
item.description: Some young non-EU families are postponing plans to have children because they now face paying for childcare in Malta. Centres catering mainly for these families fear that the budgets withdrawal of free childcare could force them to close. Only those who obtain long-term residency after five years and completion of the I Belong integration programme remain eligible for the free services.
